headline: Refining windfall lifts profit and slashes net debt
summary_short: BP's underlying RC profit was $8.5B, up from $5.7B last quarter and $2.2B a year ago, with operating cash flow of $14.8B and net debt down to $13.9B.
summary_long: Underlying RC profit rose on significantly higher realized refining margins and a much stronger gas marketing and trading result. Operating cash flow was $14.8B versus $7.8B a year ago. Upstream production fell to 2,220 mboe/d from 2,362. Reported profit was $4.7B after $4.1B of impairments, mainly in transition businesses. Net debt fell to $13.9B from $22.2B at year-end. Interim dividend is 8.660 cents per share. Q4 production is guided to 2,090-2,230 mboe/d.
confidence_notes: Figures from the 6-K; underlying RC profit and net debt are non-IFRS measures. Reported profit includes $4.1B pre-tax impairments. Q/Q delta for EPS omitted because prior-quarter per-ADS figure was not loaded.

drivers.explanation: Versus Q2, mainly significantly higher realized refining margins and a significantly higher gas marketing and trading result. Versus a year ago, higher refining margins and realizations.
The increase reflects the higher underlying earnings in the period.
Lower spend reflects the company's decisions around capital spend.
Customers underlying result was lower on weaker fuels margins, offset by products up $2.5B on refining; oil production result slightly lower on weaker liquids realizations.
